_meta.indication: JETREA is a proteolytic enzyme indicated for the treatment of symptomatic vitreomacular adhesion.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-masked, 6-month study; single intravitreal injection of ocriplasmin 125 µg vs placebo, randomization 2:1
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with symptomatic vitreomacular adhesion (focal VMA leading to symptoms)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of patients with non-surgical resolution of focal VMA at Day 28 post-injection, determined by masked CRC OCT evaluation
pivotal_trials.result: VMA resolution at Day 28: 27.9% ocriplasmin vs 13.1% placebo; difference 14.8% (95% CI: 6.0, 23.5), P=0.003

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-masked, 6-month study; single intravitreal injection of ocriplasmin 125 µg vs placebo, randomization 3:1
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with symptomatic vitreomacular adhesion (focal VMA leading to symptoms)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of patients with non-surgical resolution of focal VMA at Day 28 post-injection, determined by masked CRC OCT evaluation
pivotal_trials.result: VMA resolution at Day 28: 25.3% ocriplasmin vs 6.2% placebo; difference 19.1% (95% CI: 11.6, 26.7), P<0.001

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence 5%-20%): vitreous floaters, conjunctival hemorrhage, eye pain, photopsia, blurred vision, macular hole, reduced visual acuity, visual impairment, and retinal edema. A decrease of >=3 lines of BCVA occurred in 5.6% of JETREA vs 3.2% vehicle patients; intraocular inflammation occurred in 7.1% vs 3.7%; dyschromatopsia in 2% of JETREA patients.
target_moa: Ocriplasmin has proteolytic activity against protein components of the vitreous body and the vitreoretinal interface (e.g. laminin, fibronectin and collagen), dissolving the protein matrix responsible for vitreomacular adhesion.

rems.type: REMS is not recommended for this product.

advisory_committee.vote: Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drugs Advisory Committee (July 26, 2012) voted unanimously (10 vs. 0) that 0.125 mg ocriplasmin demonstrated efficacy in treatment of VMA, and unanimously that benefits outweighed the risks.

summary.text: BLA 125422 for Jetrea (ocriplasmin) was received April 17, 2012 and granted a priority review as the first non-surgical treatment for symptomatic VMA; approval was based on two Phase 3 randomized, placebo-controlled trials (TG-MV-006 and TG-MV-007) and was supported by a unanimous Advisory Committee vote.

citations.quote: This application was received April 17, 2012, given a priority review, and the PDUFa goal date is October 17, 2012.

The application was granted a priority review, because VMA is a serious, sight-threatening disease and JETREA is the first non-surgical treatment for this condition and has the potential to offer a significant improvement to available therapies.
The Applicant submitted two pivotal studies: study TG-MV-006, and study TG-MV-007.
